At AIL, safety is not merely a priority; it is our foundational core and essence, shaping every business decision, project commissioning, and operational shift. We maintain the unwavering conviction that no production target or operational milestone is ever considered worth compromising the safety of people associated with us. AIL strives to prevent injury by sustaining an injury-free workplace with a mindset of zero tolerance towards any incident or injury. Health impact or injury during working may lead to financial implications and reputation loss to AIL. Any accident may also impact the morale of the workers leading to production losses. Non adherence to OHS requirement may also lead to fines and penalties.

We have developed and adopted a robust, comprehensive, and reliable Occupational Health and Safety Management System, process safety, risk management and Emergency mitigation system under Aarti Management System. All our employees, contract employees and visitors are covered under our management system. In addition we have implemented following safety interventions across our manufacturing locations: • Institutionalised the “Besafe+ (Dil se)” journey, shifting safety from a priority to a core value through active shop-floor involvement and tools like Personal Safety Action Plans (PSAP). • Plant-level initiatives such as daily toolbox talk, monthly awareness sessions, etc.

We are committed to a decarbonisation strategy centred on increasing the share of renewable energy within our power mix and institutionalising energy-efficient solutions across our manufacturing footprint. By systematically reducing our dependence on fossil-fuel-based energy, we aim to significantly lower our Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions while enhancing resource productivity. This transition not only supports a cleaner environment but also drives long-term cost optimisation and reinforces our operational resilience.

We have regularised usage of Biomass for replacing coal gradually in order to reduce carbon emissions. We have several energy efficiency programmes through process optimisation. Under this, one such programme is to recover energy from a distillation condenser in the form of steam by supplying hot water, this enables us to save cooling water loss and recover energy saving fuels and eliminating CO2 emissions. We have adopted an IT-based Energy Management System (EnMS) for controlling, managing and conserving energy. Based on our several energy efficiency initiatives, we have saved approx 2.3 million KWH of energy in FY 2025-26. AIL has started receiving 13.2 MW of hybrid renewable energy. Additionally 2.75 MW of renewable energy is also sourced since Q3 FY26. Further phase-2 investment for 25.7.MW is expected to be operational in FY 2026-27.

At AIL, we recognise our workforce as our most vital intellectual asset and the cornerstone of our organisational resilience. Our long-term growth trajectory is linked to a robust human capital strategy that prioritises the identification, development, and preservation of high-potential talent. By institutionalising rigorous recruitment standards, providing continuous upskilling through training, we align our people’s professional aspirations with the Company’s strategic objectives.

We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and equitable work environment that prioritises the physical and psychological well-being of our workforce. By cultivating a high-performance culture rooted in our value of care and employee engagement, we ensure that organisational growth is aligned with individual professional development. This is supported by a robust framework for continuous capacity building and skill upgradation, alongside welfare benefits designed to enhance the quality of life for all our employees.

Human rights considerations are intrinsic to our entire value chain, from upstream raw material procurement to downstream distribution. We view the protection of human rights as a material priority, as any oversight could lead to significant regulatory non-compliance and localised reputational risks. Consequently, integrating human rights due diligence into our internal and external operations is vital to maintaining our social license to operate.

We have developed a robust Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) framework to facilitate the systematic assessment of our operational footprint. As part of this commitment, we conduct site-specific vulnerability assessments to proactively identify, mitigate, and monitor human rights risks. This culture of accountability is extended across our entire value chain; we mandate that our business partners align with our human rights policies, a requirement strictly formalised through our contractual agreements.

Risk: Exposure to physical risks from extreme climate events potentially leading to operational disruptions and asset loss, alongside transition risks arising from tightening environmental regulations that may impact market reputation and compliance costs. Opportunity: AIL perceives the shift toward a green economy as an opportunity to enhance operational efficiency. Capitalising on decarbonisation pathways through the adoption of low-carbon technologies and fostering strategic industrial synergies to drive innovation in sustainable chemical manufacturing.

AIL has institutionalised climate governance by defining clear roles and responsibilities for managing climate-related risks and opportunities. Water availability is a material physical risk, where scarcity could disrupt manufacturing continuity and revenue generation. We also acknowledge the environmental and regulatory risks associated with potential water resource contamination or habitat degradation due to treatment failures.

We are committed to water stewardship, ensuring resource availability for both our operations and neighbouring communities through strategic CSR interventions. Eight manufacturing facilities are Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) compliant, three are ZLD ready, and the rest are progressing toward ZLD readiness. By mainstreaming resource circularity—specifically through the recovery of condensate and RO permeate—we are effectively decoupling production growth from freshwater demand while reducing the hydraulic load on our Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs). Furthermore, we are evaluating next-generation adiabatic reaction technologies to minimise water loss within our cooling systems, driving long-term operational resilience.

Our operational waste streams comprise both hazardous and non-hazardous materials. We recognise that any deviations from prescribed disposal protocols present significant environmental, regulatory, and compliance risks, which may result in legal sanctions or financial penalties. Consequently, we prioritise stringent waste management to ensure absolute adherence to statutory requirements.

Our waste management approach is systematically divided into three priorities depending upon the various operating conditions and type of waste generated. Our priority to reduce hazardous wastes are: A. First Priority: Produce less hazardous waste a. Change industrial process to eliminate use of harmful chemicals b. Use less hazardous product c. Reduce packaging materials in products d. Change industrial processes to reduce or eliminate hazardous waste production B. Second Priority: Convert hazardous waste to less hazardous or non - hazardous substance by using 4 R’s a. Reuse b. Recovery c. Recycle d. Repair C. Last Priority – Treatment & disposal of all our waste: a. Treating waste to reduce toxicity b. Auditing of Hazardous waste Handlers. c. Incinerate waste d. Waste in landfills
